synopsis: Residual risk remains after protective measures; ALARP requires further reduction unless its cost in money, time or trouble is grossly disproportionate to the benefit, with proportionality judged rather than calculated by a formula [f12138, f12143, f12144]. Australia's model WHS regulation 215 requires powered mobile plant collision risk to be controlled so far as reasonably practicable and requires a warning device [f2783]. Collision warning or avoidance technology cannot cover every situation, and failure-free testing does not prove zero risk; the program also faces risks from unnecessary stops and uncertainty from relying on simulation [f3646, f12150, f12149]. Which residual risks cannot credibly be represented virtually remains unresolved, so assessor-quality evidence should explicitly state residual risks and what simulation does not establish [f1973, f8054]. The proposed evidence chain ends in a residual-risk decision, with a single “golden thread” tracing one requirement from a real test through the model and virtual result to that decision [f10795, f10919]. Acceptance needs a named person or board and a documented disposition of unresolved risks; although deadline pressure can encourage acceptance, launch should depend on unresolved safety evidence rather than the calendar [f12139, f11136, f12151, f12152].
